newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia eyes $138 mln tax lien sale - paper.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia eyes $138 mln tax lien sale - paper.

text.p: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell is considering selling about 90,000 property tax liens and expects to generate about $138 million from the deal, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Friday.
Proceeds from the sale, the first of its kind for Philadelphia, would be split between the city and the Philadelphia School District.
The city is owed about $282 million in back property taxes, and about $173 million of the total would be involved in the tax-lien sale.
If approved by city council, the sale could take place in early January. A vote is expected before the December 12 council recess.
In the secondary market Friday, Philadelphia School District AMBAC 5.50s of 2015 were offered at 5.60 percent net. Kenny Evaluation Services priced the bonds at a 5.59 yield at Thursday's close.
